briefs.headline: Risk-off: stocks lower, led by chips and AI names, as Tesla, Meta and Lam Research earnings failed to impress and oil pushed toward $100 on Saudi attacks and reports of planned US-Israel strikes on Iran.

data.name: Initial jobless claims (wk 10/17)
data.read: lowest since July; low-fire labor market
data.reaction: futures held ~-1% S&P / -1.6% NDX; 10-yr kept sliding to ~5.05% on risk-off

drivers: AI-trade fatigue: Tesla cut 2026 capex to about $20B from about $25B and fell about 5% pre-market before paring; Meta beat on revenue but booked a roughly $10B legal charge and narrowed capex to $135-145B, shares down about 6% early. Lam Research fell 7-10% on a supply-constrained outlook; SOX -3% with NVDA, AMD, INTC and MRVL all lower.

Oil: Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure, the State Dept ordering non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia, and a NYT report of a short but intensive US-Israel operation against Iran after the midterms. Brent hit a five-month high near $112; WTI near $99.
Rates and Fed: FOMC is in blackout ahead of Oct 27-28; FedWatch prices about 87% odds of a hold, with a December hike widely expected. Yields are falling today on risk-off flows, not on the data.
Overseas: Asia sold off hard (Nikkei -2.7%, Hang Seng -3.0%, KOSPI -3.5%, Taiwan -1.8%); Europe lower (Stoxx 600 -0.6%, CAC -1.3%, DAX -0.5%) after a hot UK CPI print of 3.5%.
